video_title: Miles Bridges to Phoenix, Kawhi-Raptors/Mavericks, LeBron's Future & More | Third Apron Podcast

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: Phoenix Suns trade a 2033 first-round pick to the Hornets
quotes.excerpt: They're trading a 2033 first-round pick to the Hornets in exchange they're getting Miles Bridges
quotes.quote: They're trading a 2033 first-round pick to the Hornets in exchange they're getting Miles Bridges, a crappy 2029 first-round pick, a 2027 second-round pick, they're getting off the negative salaries of Royce O'Neale and Grayson Allen, and $30 million in immediate tax savings.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Quinn's evaluation of Miles Bridges as a player
quotes.excerpt: I am lower on him than I think everybody in Phoenix. I do not think he is a winning player.
quotes.quote: I am lower on him than I think everybody in Phoenix. I do not think he is a winning player. I think he is somebody who is a lot better in theory than he actually is in practice. Given his athletic tools, he has never been the defender that he should be. He has been an above-average three-point shooter once in his career. I know he can do stuff with the ball in his hands, but he is on a team now with Devin Booker and Jalen Green and Colin Gillespie and Dillon Brooks, a lot of guys who want to have the ball. I don't know how much mileage you're going to get out of that.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Miles Bridges' shooting statistics with LaMelo Ball
quotes.excerpt: With LaMelo Ball on the floor, Miles Bridges' true shooting is just under 61%.
quotes.quote: Over the last two years, with LaMelo Ball on the floor, Miles Bridges' true shooting is just under 61%. With LaMelo Ball off of the floor, it's just over 51%. That is an enormous drop. I just don't believe Miles Bridges is a good enough player to justify giving away a draft pick this valuable.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA teams are devaluing draft picks in the 20s
quotes.excerpt: Teams don't really want picks in the 20s anymore because all of the best prospects go back to college.
quotes.quote: Teams don't really want picks in the 20s anymore because all of the best prospects go back to college for NIL and you're just stuck with a guaranteed salary for somebody who's probably a prospect in the 30s or the 40s, rather than a top-20 caliber prospect. Those picks just are not that valuable.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: Toronto Raptors' interest in trading Brandon Ingram
quotes.excerpt: The Raptors are looking to ideally trade Brandon Ingram over RJ Barrett and one future first-round pick.
quotes.quote: The Raptors are looking to ideally trade Brandon Ingram over RJ Barrett and one future first-round pick. It sounds like the Raptors are trying to get Kawhi Leonard for a similar package like they did last time.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Why the Toronto Raptors should prefer Brandon Ingram over RJ Barrett
quotes.excerpt: If it's Brandon Ingram as the centerpiece salary of this trade, that makes it much easier to trade more.
quotes.quote: If it's Brandon Ingram as the centerpiece salary of this trade, that makes it much easier to trade more than Kawhi Leonard's $50.3 million salary, which is going to be important because as we've talked about, when you trade less money than you take back, you trigger a hard cap at the first apron, which the Raptors can't really deal with.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: The Toronto Raptors' strategy for future trades
quotes.excerpt: I would not put Colin Murray-Boyles on the table under any circumstances whatsoever.
quotes.quote: I would not put Colin Murray-Boyles on the table under any circumstances whatsoever. You trade two firsts now, one of those conveys, and in a few years you have three picks and a few swaps to trade with. And at that point Colin Murray-Boyles is closer to his prime, you have some of these bad contracts falling off your books, or closer to the end, and then you make another trade at that point.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: The Los Angeles Clippers' need for a starting guard
quotes.excerpt: The Clippers should go get a new starting guard and that's been something that a lot of people have been discussing.
quotes.quote: The Clippers should go get a new starting guard and that's been something that a lot of people have been discussing, which would probably revolve around Jalen Green. Not only could they potentially get a guard for Jalen Green and maybe they have to include their two tradeable first-round picks, which aren't of much value, but that could be another way for them to save money.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Ja Morant as a potential trade target for the Clippers
quotes.excerpt: The obvious one would be Ja Morant, which would not save them much money, but you could nearly match with Jalen Green and then Haywood Highsmith.
quotes.quote: The obvious one would be Ja Morant, which would not save them much money, but you could nearly match with Jalen Green and then Haywood Highsmith. Would they have enough room under the first apron to do that and then fill out the team?

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Why the Clippers should target Dejounte Murray
quotes.excerpt: If we're talking about going cheaper, the next one down the list is probably Dejounte Murray with the Pelicans.
quotes.quote: If we're talking about going cheaper, the next one down the list is probably Dejounte Murray with the Pelicans. Do they have enough tax room to do Jalen Green for Dejounte Murray straight up?

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: The Los Angeles Lakers' interest in LeBron James
quotes.excerpt: Kevin O'Connor posted an article about the Warriors being interested in getting to the clutch business, wanting to bring in LeBron James.
quotes.quote: Kevin O'Connor posted an article about the Warriors being interested in getting to the clutch business, wanting to bring in LeBron James, bringing in Anthony Davis. And my initial reaction when I read this was that the Warriors more easily could have done this at the trade deadline. I'm not saying it was up to them, it was probably not up to them. It seems like LeBron was not ready to get traded yet, Lakers weren't ready to trade LeBron, but it would have been far easier to get this done because the Warriors could have easily just swapped Jimmy Butler for LeBron.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green's potential pay cut and future with the Warriors
quotes.excerpt: he declines at 27 and then he resigns at 20 for multiple years

text_blocks.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
text_blocks.text: What would make sense for Draymond Green? Is there a 25% discount he can take off that and then do a longer-term deal?

text_blocks.speaker: Sam Quinn
text_blocks.text: The obvious would be something like what you are suggesting where he declines at 27 and then he resigns at 20 for multiple years. The other thing too is that Draymond is such a fixture and there is probably enough trust with that organization where he could do the Dirk thing where he has an unofficial role with the team after he retires where he is kind of maybe hypothetically made whole after the fact.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green potentially taking a pay cut to help the Warriors
quotes.excerpt: if they think they have a real chance at LeBron, maybe Draymond does the James Harden thing

text_blocks.speaker: Sam Quinn
text_blocks.text: What I wouldn't be surprised, if they think they have a real chance at LeBron, maybe Draymond does the James Harden thing where he declines the option, he goes into free agency and he just says, spend the money that you are going to spend and I will take what is left.

text_blocks.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
text_blocks.text: I don't know how far down Draymond is willing to go. I don't think he is taking like $10 million, but I think if you are getting LeBron and AD, he probably be willing to work with you.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: The uncertainty surrounding Kristaps Porzingis's contract extension
quotes.excerpt: do you have to go above the mid-level to keep him?

text_blocks.speaker: Sam Quinn
text_blocks.text: We also don't know what Kristaps Porzingis is resigning for. Do you have to go above the mid-level to keep him?

text_blocks.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
text_blocks.text: I think they would by not too much.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: Trading Moses Moody to fit Kristaps Porzingis's salary
quotes.excerpt: trading Moses Moody to fit Porzingis on more money

text_blocks.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
text_blocks.text: I think the move after then would be trading Moses Moody to fit Porzingis on more money. So then they are like $5 million below the first apron. He has got these incentives. So can you get Porzingis back on 17 and a half?

text_blocks.speaker: Sam Quinn
text_blocks.text: I would assume. I don't know who is topping that.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: The risk of relying on Yaxel Lendeborg as a rookie
quotes.excerpt: you are making a pretty big bet on a rookie there

text_blocks.speaker: Sam Quinn
text_blocks.text: You are also really relying on Yaxel Lendeborg to defend the ball a lot as a rookie. I know that is what he does well, that is what he did at Michigan, but like you are making a pretty big bet on a rookie there. I know Draymond can defend a Porzingis-type stars when you really get to crunch time, but over 82 games, you kind of need somebody like Moody just to throw at opposing ball handlers.

text_blocks.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
text_blocks.text: I guess you are saying that Yaxel will do it. I am a big, big Yaxel guy, maybe he can, but that is a big bet to make on a rookie.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: The trade value of Anthony Davis versus Jimmy Butler
quotes.excerpt: are we sure Anthony Davis with two years left on supermax money is a more valuable asset

text_blocks.speaker: Sam Quinn
text_blocks.text: Are we sure Anthony Davis with two years left on supermax money is a more valuable asset than Jimmy Butler with one year left at supermax money, even with Jimmy Butler on the torn ACL? Because we both think Anthony Davis is a bad contract, right?

text_blocks.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
text_blocks.text: Yeah, probably. There is so much we don't know so I was thinking about it.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: The risk of trading for Jimmy Butler after his injury
quotes.excerpt: I would rather just wait until January, get Jimmy back and deal with his contract

text_blocks.speaker: Sam Quinn
text_blocks.text: I trust him enough that when he comes back, he is going to be a productive player, that I would rather just wait until January, get Jimmy back and deal with his contract in the off-season, than take on Anthony Davis who is angling for an extension. There is no universe in which I would extend Anthony Davis to be absolutely clear about this.

text_blocks.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
text_blocks.text: I just I think this trade only happens if the Wizards are getting genuinely positive value for Anthony Davis.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers' potential cap space and roster needs
quotes.excerpt: they might be a team interested in giving Peyton Watson a very big offer sheet

text_blocks.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
text_blocks.text: Seems like they want to use cap space. Steinline was reporting that they are might be a team interested in giving Peyton Watson a very big offer sheet. And then there was another report, I want to say The Athletic, that they might be a team interested in Cam Johnson.

text_blocks.speaker: Sam Quinn
text_blocks.text: If the Clippers were to trade Kawhi for Jimmy with picks involved of course, I think the Clippers would get a lot out of Jimmy.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: The Rockets' potential interest in Marcus Smart
quotes.excerpt: Rockets being the team linked to Marcus Smart and I think there is a three-year offer

text_blocks.speaker: Sam Quinn
text_blocks.text: Rockets being the team linked to Marcus Smart and I think there is a three-year offer that Mark Stein says. I don't know that they should go back to the Lakers well after Dorian Finney-Smith last year.

text_blocks.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
text_blocks.text: That is interesting a three-year offer because I am a little surprised by that amount.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: Marcus Smart's potential role and contract with the Rockets
quotes.excerpt: if you get Smart, you don't have to make him play the one

text_blocks.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
text_blocks.text: If you get Smart, you don't have to make him play the one. You can have him play off-ball with the other guards and maybe even play up to the three which he has done with the Lakers.

text_blocks.speaker: Sam Quinn
text_blocks.text: I suppose it is just I don't know. I am starting to really disagree with some of the decisions the Rockets are making lately.
